title: Find potential customers from their public complaints
summary: A founder had Claude Code search 40 posts complaining about coding tools and pull 5 matching profiles with contact details, reporting a total cost of $0.02.
agent_role: Claude Code, using a social search service, found complaint posts, picked relevant profiles and gathered their public contact details. The human set the goal.
outcome: The author reports the whole search cost $0.02 and replaced manual digging and a paid lead tool.
what_they_did: The poster connected Claude Code to a social search service called treg_ai. They asked it to find posts from people complaining about Cursor, Claude Code and Codex. The agent searched 40 posts, then picked 5 relevant profiles and collected their available contact details.
how_it_went: The author says the whole search cost $0.02, with no lead-finding subscription and no hours of manual profile browsing.
prompt: Search public social posts from the last [time period] where people complain about [problem or competitor products]. Collect about [number] posts. From those, pick the [number] authors most likely to need [your product], explain why for each, and list any contact details they have made public. Put the results in a table with post link, summary of the complaint, and contact info. Do not message anyone; show me the list first so I can decide who to contact.

curation.rationale: A real multi-step lead-finding run with a concrete cost figure, but thin on steps and it doubles as a nod to a specific search service.
